theme_scores.justification: The Pension Schemes Act 2015 power inserting Part 1A into JUPRA is cited as the route to mirror JUPRA, and the 1 April 2017 target and no-delay decision are stated, but no uncited evidence or Reference/Link shows why the timetable or litigation stance was chosen.

theme_scores.theme: Interim and retrospective payments to retired members
theme_scores.justification: The 13 December 2015 Employment Tribunal judgment is named as confirming the Preston formula and the interim payment basis is explained, but no reference or link is given and the regulation text only describes the mechanism.

theme_scores.theme: Recovery of historic contributions and ancillary scheme windows
theme_scores.justification: The contribution rate tables, recovery routes and option windows (regs 53-58, 78, 103-116) describe the measures, and the MoJ-HMRC discussion and the respondent's list of elements are assertions or positions, with no evidence of why the rates or time limits were set or that they will work.

The Employment Appeal Tribunal outcome and the MoJ proposals to the Tribunal are mentioned without citation or any evidence for the chosen cut-off dates, and the decision on how to give effect is explicitly deferred with no method.

reasoning: The four core themes score 1, 1, 0 and 0, a mean of 0.5, which rounds to 1. Legislative route and timetable names the Pension Schemes Act 2015 as the source of the Lord Chancellor's power ("the MoJ has used the Pension Schemes Act 2015 to insert a new Part 1A in JUPRA") and the aim to start by 1 April 2017 without waiting for litigation. That is a legal route with some explanation, but the document gives no reference and does not explain why this timetable was chosen over alternatives. Interim payments relies on the "judgment of 13 December 2015" confirming the Preston formula and explains how the interim payments and later true-up work. It carries no reference or link, so it stays at level 1. Historic contributions sets out detailed rate tables and windows, but as descriptions of measures with no evidence that the rates or time limits work as intended. Unresolved cases defers decisions with "will provide a further update in due course" and names tribunals and cut-off dates without a source. The strongest counter-example to a score of 1 is that the section could be read as level 0, since the mean of 0.5 depends on two thinly evidenced themes. To reach level 2 the document would need to cite the Employment Tribunal judgments and the Act with references or links, explain why the 2017 date and the cut-off dates were chosen, and give the basis and costing for the contribution rates and option windows. Level 3 would require the document itself to assess the uncertainties.
